evals.prompt: I am a resident individual. I bought a plot of land in May 2015 and sold it in October 2026. Which LTCG rate applies, and can I still use indexation?
expectations: Says the default long-term rate is 12.5% without indexation
Explains that for land or buildings acquired before 23 July 2024, a resident individual or HUF may instead have the tax computed at 20% with indexation, and pays the lower of the two
Does not say indexation is available for every asset or abolished with no exception for this plot

evals.prompt: Two sales in the same year. (a) A plot I bought on 2024-09-10 and sold on 2026-11-20. (b) Unlisted company shares I bought on 2024-10-01 and sold on 2026-08-01. Give the holding period class, the tax treatment and whether indexation is possible for each.
expectations: Treats (a) as long term, because it was held more than 24 months, taxed at 12.5% with no indexation and no option, because it was acquired after 22 July 2024
Treats (b) as short term, because unlisted shares need more than 24 months, so the gain is taxed at slab rates and not at 12.5%
Does not apply the 12-month listed-share threshold to either asset

evals.prompt: I sold a flat for ₹1,00,00,000. In scenario A the stamp duty value is ₹1,08,00,000; in scenario B it is ₹1,12,00,000. What full value of consideration do I use for capital gains in each?
expectations: Scenario A: the stamp duty value is within 110% of the actual price, so the actual ₹1,00,00,000 is used
Scenario B: the stamp duty value exceeds 110%, so the whole stamp duty value of ₹1,12,00,000 is used, not only the excess
must_match: (?i)(within|up to|under|below|inside|less than|lower than|does not exceed|doesn't exceed|not more than|not exceed)[^.]{0,60}110\s?%

evals.prompt: I sold land held for 6 years. Net sale consideration after expenses is ₹2,00,00,000 and the long-term gain is ₹1,00,00,000. I bought one residential house for ₹80,00,000 within a year. How much is exempt under section 54F, and how much is taxable?
expectations: Computes the exemption proportionally: gain x cost of new house / net consideration = ₹40,00,000
Concludes ₹60,00,000 remains taxable as long-term gain
Does not treat the ₹80,00,000 cost of the house as the exempt amount
must_not_match: (?i)\bexempt(ion)? amount (is|=|equals|will be|would be) ₹?\s?(80,00,000|80 lakh)|\b(exempt(ion)?|amount exempt) (is|=|equals) ₹?\s?(80,00,000|80 lakh)

evals.prompt: I sold land on 2026-08-12 with a long-term gain of ₹80,00,000. I put ₹20,00,000 into REC bonds on 2026-12-15 and plan to put ₹60,00,000 into NHAI bonds on 2027-03-01 for section 54EC. How much is exempt, and what are the limits?
expectations: States the investment must be made within six months of the transfer, so the 2027-03-01 NHAI investment is too late
Only the ₹20,00,000 REC investment qualifies, so ₹60,00,000 stays taxable
States the ₹50 lakh limit and the five-year lock-in
must_match: (?i)(60,00,000|60 lakh|0\.6 crore)[^.]{0,60}(taxable|not exempt|taxed|not eligible|not qualify|chargeable)|(taxable|chargeable|taxed)[^.]{0,60}(60,00,000|60 lakh|0\.6 crore)

evals.prompt: All three are land sales by a resident individual, after 1 April 2026. (a) Bought 2024-09-10, sold 2026-09-10. (b) Bought 2024-09-10, sold 2026-09-11. (c) Bought 2024-07-23, sold 2026-12-01. For each, is the gain short term or long term, and may I choose 20% with indexation?
expectations: (a) is short term because exactly 24 months is not more than 24 months, so slab rates apply and the indexation option never arises
(b) is long term at 12.5% with no indexation option, because it was acquired after 22 July 2024
(c) is long term but was acquired on 23 July 2024, not before it, so there is no 20% indexed option and the rate is 12.5%
